I've been trying to find a good, cheap tablet. It doesn't need to retail for $50--if you find one that's discounted to $50 or less then that would be fine too, feel free to share.

Also, are there any brands to avoid?

EDIT: Thanks for the advice, everyone. I ended up buying a Huion that was on sale for $40. To protect myself, I threw in a 3-year warranty, so I should be OK if it turns out to be crappy/broken/etc.
What's the best drawing tablet for under $50? Are there any brands to avoid in general?

I'd recomend a Wacom. I'm in the UK though so I can't say how much they might be where you are, but the Wacom Pen & Touch I've had for the last three years or so has been great. It was about £65 when I bought it new (though to be honest I've never really used the touch feature). You can pick up the standard model without touch pretty cheap on eBay.

50 or less is a bit of a stretch. I use a Vistablet v12 which runs around $80 new right now so you MIGHT find one floating around used for less. Its cheap, works well, and has more than double the active drawing space of a Wacom of similar price.

Monoprice. Good stuff cheap. http://www.monoprice.com/Category?c_id=113&cp_id=11303

My SO uses one of their tablets and is impressed with it.
I also have a Monoprice. It functions well enough, but it lacks polish. The pen, drawing surface, and buttons are all just "okay." But you can still create incredible stuff with it.
I've been looking at Monoprice, but some reviewers say they've had serious problems. Thanks for the suggestion though, they may be who I go with.
It can be a hit or miss with some of their stuff. but they are pretty good at fixing any issues. We have several items from them and can report no problems so far.
I got one from Aldi, it works fine and it was very well priced at $59.95.

Don't bother with cheap. Get a wacom. Get an old model to save money instead of an off brand, they take time to get used to but are awesome. Don't cripple yourself with a our experience. I've owned 3 so far, currently using a big ish intuos pro. My favorite was the bamboo 2 with touch sensor. It was only a small one but it was perfect even with 2 21" screens
